findings.finding: Yorkville (YA II PN) holds $5.05m of convertible debentures maturing January to April 2027 and all 1,401 preferred shares; against an equity of about $2.5m that is standing conversion supply which can be exercised and sold on any day, the window included; the 2026-09-08 13D puts 700 preferred at 21m ordinary-share equivalents, subject to a 4.99% blocker.
findings.mechanism_in_window: A conversion notice needs no scheduled date or filing and can be delivered and sold on 2026-10-07. It is a standing capacity, not a dated event, and the 10-Q's flat share count (1,424,834 on 2026-08-01 and 2026-08-31) shows no conversions recently, so it is sized small.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No conversion-driven move can be identified in the record: the 10-Q reports no preferred conversions in H1 2026, and the share count did not change through August.
findings.why_not_priced: The overhang is public, so its level is known. What the price does not hold is whether Yorkville uses a two-day 45% drawdown to convert at a discount and sell. A priced overhang would show the stock no longer trading on the late-September squeeze. It is still well above Alpine Fox's $1.18 cost, so a conversion seller still has room.
